newsitem.title: Japan: Boom in Japan PC sales cooling.
newsitem.headline: Boom in Japan PC sales cooling.

text.p: After growing a staggering 70 percent in fiscal 1996, personal computer sales in Japan are likely to grow at a much slower rate in the year ending in March, industry officials and analysts said Tuesday.
"The basic undertone is steady expansion, but the fact is things have shifted into cruising speed," said Mami Indo, analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research.

Some analysts cut their fiscal 1997 sales forecasts after a disappointing Christmas season and now expect slower PC sales for the year to the end of March. Christmas sales in 1995 got a boost from the introduction of new Windows 95 software.

PC makers, which suffered from cut-throat price wars in 1995, are now focusing more on profits rather than sales, and decided late last year not to introduce low-priced PCs aimed at consumers, officials said.
"It only reflects a change in their sales strategy," said Kazushi Shiga, analyst at Dataquest, adding that sales growth will boom again once makers start producing lower-cost models.
Japanese PC makers include Toshiba Corp., NEC Corp. and Fujitsu Ltd.
Shiga expects growth of about 30 percent for Japanese PC sales for the fiscal year through March, down slightly from an earlier estimate.
Tetsuya Mizoguchi, the head of the Japan Electronic Industry Development Association's PC division, said a delay in the launch of new models has affected the sales trend.
A delay in the launch of PCs fitted with Intel Corp.'s new MMX chip, designed to enhanced graphics, audio and video on the machines, has also curtailed demand, he said.
Shortages of new liquid-crystal displays and longer-life batteries also put restraints on sales of laptop and notebook computers, he said.
Mizoguchi said domestic PC sales may fall short of the association's target of 7.5 million units in the fiscal year ending in March.
But the following year, shipments are expected to rise about 24 percent to ship about 9.3 million units, the association said.
"We expect some favourable factors to support sales next year, such as the introduction of Windows NT 4.0 software," Mizoguchi said.
